transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I’m here because... for almost two years now, I’ve been completely unable to shake this certainty that a few people in the ensemble are quietly undermining my work. It really started right after that big commission I had. Which, honestly, was such a massive undertaking. I was practically living in the studio, and the heating in that building was completely broken for
Aside from feeling that others are undermining you, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. The only things I hear are... well, just normal sounds, you know? 

Actually, speaking of sounds, the acoustics in that studio were completely unforgiving. Because it was an old pre-war building, the pipes would make this awful groaning noise right in the middle of a recording take. And there was this bakery on the first floor—great sourdough, honestly, I used to get a loaf every Tuesday—but their ventilation fan would just drone on and on, right up through the floorboards. I emailed the landlord about it, like, five times, asking if we could at least split the cost of some acoustic paneling, but he just completely ghosted me. Typical, right? He's the same guy who wouldn't fix the heat. 

But anyway... no. No imaginary voices or anything. Just really annoying real noises.

Before this situation with the commission started about two years ago, would you say you were generally trusting of colleagues and friends, or have you always tended to be wary and suspicious of other people's motives, even going back to your teens or twenties?

No, not at all. I mean, before all this started, I was always pretty trusting. Very collaborative, honestly. Back in grad school, I had this totally open-door policy with my cohort. 

Actually, my roommate then, David—he was a cellist—we used to share everything. He bought this massive, vintage chrome espresso machine at a thrift store that took up, like, our entire tiny kitchen counter. We spent probably three weeks just trying to find a replacement gasket for the portafilter because the company went out of business in the eighties. He eventually had to order a custom silicone one from this obscure parts dealer in Milan. It took forever to ship. And then when it finally worked, it made incredibly bitter coffee, honestly, just pulled the worst, most over-extracted shots, but he was so proud of it. We'd stay up drinking that awful espresso and just bouncing composition ideas off each other until two in the morning. 

So, yeah, I never really worried about people having hidden agendas or anything back then. We were all just in it together. It’s really just been since that commission that things changed.

Over the past two years, have there been periods where your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or energetic—like needing much less sleep than usual, talking faster, or feeling like your thoughts were racing—separate from your concerns about the ensemble?

No, no, my mood's been pretty normal, honestly. I mean, I sleep fine, usually. Well, mostly fine. I did buy this new mattress recently, one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box? It was supposed to expand to full size in 24 hours, but the left corner stayed totally flat for, like, three days. I had to call customer service, and the guy on the phone—I think his name was Gary—he told me to literally jump on the corner to fluff the foam. Which, obviously, felt ridiculous. I'm a grown man jumping on a bed like a toddler. It did eventually expand, but honestly, it sleeps a little hot anyway. I kind of miss my old spring mattress. 

But no, I haven't been talking faster or feeling super energetic or anything like that. Just regular me.

Aside from your concerns about the ensemble, has this belief affected other areas of your life—like your relationships, daily functioning, or ability to work—or would you say you're able to function normally otherwise?

No, I mean, outside of this whole mess with the ensemble, things are pretty normal. I'm still functioning just fine. I meet my deadlines, I'm still composing... actually, I've been working on this new string quartet piece. I've been trying to incorporate some unconventional bowing techniques I read about in this old treatise from the 1800s. I had to hunt down a translated copy from this rare book dealer in London. The shipping took absolute ages, and when it finally arrived, the binding was all cracked. It smelled incredible, though, like dust and old paper, you know? I love that smell. I spent a whole weekend just trying to decipher the diagrams. The guy who wrote it had the most illegible handwriting, just absolute chicken scratch. 

But yeah, I keep up with my work. I still run most mornings, too. Usually down by the river. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. So, yeah, everything else is fine. Just that one issue.
